newsitem.title: USA: Wells Rich and BDDP find buyer.
newsitem.headline: Wells Rich and BDDP find buyer.

text.p: French ad agency BDDP and its U.S. unit, Wells Rich Greene, Thursday announced a deal to be taken over by British marketing company GGT Group Inc., ending a long hunt for a buyer of the debt ridden agency.

International advertising and marketing services company GGT Group Plc said it had agreed with a majority of French advertising group BDDP's shareholders to buy the company for the equivalent of 105 million British pounds ($164 million).
The deal prevented the breakup of Wells Rich, a venerable U.S. agency founded in the ad industry's boom era in the 1960s that has struggled in the age of multinational advertising.

Wells Rich, responsible for such famed campaigns as the Alka Seltzer "Plop Plop Fizz Fizz (Oh What a Relief it is)" and Midas's "Midasize that Muffler," was rumoured to be on the verge of having its dwindling client list parceled out to other agencies.
Frank Assumma, chief executive of Wells Rich, said the acquisition means his agency will remain intact, servicing such prestigious clients as Procter & Gamble and Bristol-Myers Squibb.
GGT said in a statement the move would aim to combine the two businesses. Assumma said that there were no immediate plans for staff cutbacks at the New York office.
GGT said it had asked for its shares to be suspended pending shareholder approval and completion of the deal.
It said the deal was expected to be "significantly earnings enhancing in the first full financial year."

BDDP is France's third largest advertising agency, 15th in the United States and also holds 20 percent in Singapore-based Batey advertising network. BDDP had consolidated revenues of around 1.135 billion French francs ($221 million) in 1995.
GGT said it had revenues of 62.7 million pounds ($98 million) in the year ending April 30, 1996.
Jean-Claude Boulet and Jean-Marie Dru, senior members of the BDDP board, will join GGT as executive directors.
Walter Butler, currently president of BDDP's supervisory board, will be made a non-executive director, GGT said.
GGT said further details would be announced "as soon as possible."

"Faced with the current rapid consolidation trends in the advertising industry, the strong geographical and client complementarity between the two groups should result in an effective and smooth combination," BDDP's Butler said.

Wells Rich and BDDP were previously examined by WPP Plc, Cordiant Plc and Grey Advertising, among others, according to industy sources. BDDP and Wells Rich had also explored a leveraged buyout of the agency.
